The **2024 United States drone sightings**, also known as the **New Jersey drone sightings**, were a widespread series of reports involving unidentified drones in late 2024.
From November to December, thousands of witnesses reported seeing unmanned aerial vehicles at night.
The sightings began in New Jersey and subsequently spread to neighboring states, including New York and Pennsylvania.
Reports soon emerged across the Northeast and other parts of the country.
Investigators determined that the sightings mainly consisted of authorized drones and misidentified objects.
Sightings occurred over military installations, such as Picatinny Arsenal and Naval Weapons Station Earle, as well as civilian infrastructure and residential areas.
Notable reports included drones preventing a medical evacuation, following a Coast Guard vessel, and spraying "gray mist".
These specific incidents were later found to be commercial aircraft or atmospheric phenomena.
Other purported drones were debunked as the constellation Orion or the planet Venus.
Federal investigators examined over 5,000 reports but found no evidence of threats or anomalous activity.

A joint statement by the Department of Defense (DoD), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) concluded most sightings were authorized drones, misidentified manned aircraft, and other routine objects.
The Trump administration stated the aircraft were primarily FAA-authorized drones.
While officials confirmed unidentified drones over military bases, the DoD noted such flyovers are common and typically harmless.
Government responses included flight restrictions over sensitive areas in New York and New Jersey.
Federal and state officials received briefings on the incidents, and other authorities called for enhanced counter-drone powers and interagency coordination.
President-elect Donald Trump urged military action against unidentified drones and claimed the government had knowledge of their origins.
Misleading viral videos and images on social media added to public confusion.
Independent experts concluded that people were reacting to ordinary drones and mistaken phenomena.
Analysts such as Robert Bartholomew and Gary Small described the event as a social or mass panic, comparable to earlier episodes in American history.
Others cited factors such as confirmation bias or social contagion as contributing to the wave of reports.
Alternative explanations for the sightings, such as military operations or a search for nuclear material, received little support.

The White House confirmed that President Biden was aware of the drone sightings on December 10, 2024.[3] The next day, Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas briefed New Jersey Governor Phil Murphy and the state's Congressional delegation on the sightings.[23][32][113] In his first comments on December 18, President Biden said there was no sign of danger or anything suspicious happening, though officials continued tracking the situation amid heavy authorized drone activity in the area.
